_: The three doors: the site arranged by what a visitor came to do, rather than by which repository a page came from. Membership only; every title and description is read from lib/pages.ts, the manifest or the docs tree, so a page is named in one place. A path may sit behind two doors (a tool is both a thing to watch and a thing to build on) and that is the point: a door is a way in, not a folder.
measured: Which pages exist, and how many doors lead to each, is measured by scripts/crawl-site.py and shown at /style/map.

doors.name: Watch it run
doors.what: The machines, running in the page. Nothing here is a recording: every frame, every trace and every byte is computed while you look at it, on models built from the chips' own transistors.

doors.name: Read how it was done
doors.what: The story and the record. The arc first, then the long reads, then the notebook: every plan written before the work and every report written after it, with the figures they were written from.

doors.name: Build on it
doors.what: The parts you can use: a chip that answers over HTTP, a cartridge format, a registry that re-runs what it publishes, and the bytes from a real Geiger tube.
